messages:
support_jen: FYI getting an escalation from a customer (acme-retail) — multiple 5xx and gateway timeouts hitting hosted inference endpoints since ~10:12 UTC. They report spikes in latency to >10s and intermittent 502/504. I have request ids and a short repro.
support_jen: customer provided trace: request_id=rc-98765, 502 gateway_error, backend timeout after 15s. They tried 5 different model routes, same behaviour.
cust_ops_mike: we saw the same in the portal — token consumption unchanged but error rate jumped from 0.2% to 14% at 10:11 UTC. Top routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat.
eng_oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2028-0412-redis-cache-outage. Assigned: @infra. Pager sent.
infra_sam: pinging infra — looking at cache metrics. Redis cluster us-west-2-a shows elevated latency and rejected commands. CPU 98% on primary, replication lag ~3s.
infra_redis_bot: Redis alerts: ERR_CMD_QUEUE_FULL threshold breached on shard-3. Eviction rate high, RDB saves delayed.
eng_runtime_maya: if KV/prefix cache is blocked we can see request handlers block waiting on cache get and cause thread starvation -> 502/504. Are we seeing long tail on cache GET?
infra_sam: yes. avg GET 1.2s, p99 ~ 6.8s. Before spike was p99 12ms. Memory used at 93%. OOM events in kernel logs for one node earlier.
support_jen: customer supplied a minimal repro curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REQ_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-*-redwood","input":"hi","cache_prefix":"acme-2028-A"}'
```
They said removing cache_prefix avoided the 5xx.
cust_ops_mike: that's a key hint — prefix caching traffic appears correlated. Could be a hot prefix causing eviction storms/too many keys per prefix.
eng_runtime_maya: can we check cache miss rate and hotspot keys? Also show prefix TTLs.
infra_sam: running quick queries: top keyspace by requests shows prefix "acme-2028-A:*" accounted for 42% of GETs in last 10m. Hot keys count increased rapidly. Looks like a traffic pattern change from the customer -> causing backend to thrash.
infra_sam: I’m moving shard-3 to read-only? trying to failover. Triggering controlled failover now.
eng_runtime_maya: while failover happens we should enable fail-open at the runtime layer for that customer route (skip cache, serve from model). Config patch coming.
support_lead_anna: please loop in cust_ops and advise customer to pause heavy batch jobs if possible. We need an ETA for remediation.
infrastructure log snippet (from host rdb-03):
```
Mar 12 10:09:23 rdb-03 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12234 (redis-server)
Mar 12 10:09:24 redis[12234]: Background saving aborted by signal 9
Mar 12 10:10:02 redis[12234]: Slow command: 1.2s GET acme-2028-A:session:abcd
```
infra_sam: failover complete to standby (rdb-05). New primary accepting writes. Latency improving but still elevated due to backlog.
eng_runtime_maya: rolled canary: disabled prefix cache for acme-retail using runtime override rule id=rc-disable-cache-1805. This will avoid cache path for future requests and should reduce blocking calls.
support_jen: notified customer: asked to rerun their failing request.
cust_ops_mike: customer confirms initial success on one request, latency ~420ms and no 502. They still see intermittent 504 on some older connections.
eng_runtime_maya: those might be in-flight requests that hit blocked worker threads — should drain. We also need to patch redis client pool config to set timeouts and circuit breaker (fail fast) for GETs. Current client waits up to 10s before error. Recommend reducing to 250ms with exponential backoff.
infra_sam: filed infra ticket INFRA-7398 to tune client and add per-prefix request limiting on proxy layer.
support_lead_anna: escalation notes for account team: impact window ~10:11-10:30 UTC, ~1500 requests affected, primary cause: hot prefix from customer causing Redis node OOM and command queue saturation. Remediation: failover, disable prefix cache, tune client timeouts, add circuit breaker, and implement per-prefix throttling.
eng_runtime_maya: adding repro steps for devs: 
1) simulate hot prefix: spawn concurrent clients issuing GET/SET to acme-2028-A:*.
2) run redis mem stress tool until memory pressure causes eviction.
3) observe runtime 502/504 behavior when GETs block threadpool.
Commands used: 
```
# hammer redis with 200 concurrent clients
wrk -t8 -c200 -d120s --latency 'lua:hammer_getset.lua' http://redis-shard-3:6379
```
eng_runtime_maya: temporary mitigation PR submitted: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/842 - adds skip-cache header support and reduces redis GET timeout.
infra_sam: monitoring shows error rate falling back to baseline by 10:28. p99 cache GET now ~80ms. No further OOMs.
support_jen: customer reply: "Thanks, looks good for now. We'll throttle our job and work with you to adjust caching strategy." They requested a postmortem.
support_lead_anna: planned postmortem to include timeline, root cause (hot prefix => OOM => cmd queue full => blocked workers => 502/504), mitigation actions, and suggested customer guidance (spread prefix, use namespaced keys with low cardinality, avoid unbounded sessions keyed to user ids).
eng_oncall_bot: Reminder: allocate 2 hours for incident review and RCA doc draft.
support_jen: will draft RCA and add runbook entry: - detect prefix hotspots (alerts when one prefix >30% of cache ops), - auto-skip-cache rule per-account on failure rate, - circuit breaker for KV layer, - per-prefix rate limit at edge.
infra_sam: adding retention: captured heap snapshot and slowlog entries saved to s3://redwood-ops/INC-2028-0412/artifacts.
eng_runtime_maya: after action items: I want an automated test that injects cache latency to ensure runtime fails open and doesn't cascade. Creating ticket RUNTIME-3012.
support_jen: closing loop with customer and scheduling follow-up. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
